summary: Unexpected partner-assigned surcharge 'model-variant-rate-swap' on monthly invoice after private fallback — credit & audit CSV requested
description:
Issue summary:
Customer LexiHealth received a surprise surcharge line on their March finalized invoice tagged as 'model-variant-rate-swap:partner-account'. Charge amount: €2,340. Customer asserts all workloads ran on their Dedicated pool in eu-west and that a partner account should never be billed to their org.

Impact:
- Immediate financial impact: unexpected €2,340 charge on finalized invoice affecting customer procurement.
- Operational: customer is pausing new ingestion jobs until billing is resolved.
- Reputational: customer is requesting an audit CSV and explanation within 48 hours to avoid escalation to legal.

Environment:
- Customer tier: Dedicated (reserved GPUs, committed monthly pool).
- Deployment: Private fallback configured to route to Redwood partner-account (billing mapping) as a temporary overflow during maintenance windows.
- Region: eu-west.
- Time window of interest: 2026-02-28 22:15:00 — 2026-03-01 03:10:00 UTC (span includes nightly maintenance).
steps_to_reproduce:
1) LexiHealth sent high-throughput batch embed job (multi-model) starting 2026-02-28 22:18 UTC.
2) Dedicated pool reported capacity contention at 22:20 and routing decision triggered fallback policy 'private-to-partner-overflow' (intended to be disabled for this org).
3) Some requests were routed to a partner-owned capacity pool which carries different rate rules.
4) Postback metering tagged those requests with partner billing keys and they were aggregated into the March billing run.

Customer says they did not opt in to partner overflow. Steps to reproduce internally: review routing trace for LexiHealth org id during window, check routing policy flags, and inspect billing attribution logs for routed requests.
logs:
- Routing traces (sample): trace_id=tr-9f2b, org=lexi-1004, route=partner-overflow, selected_pool=partner-eu-1, timestamp=2026-02-28T22:20:12Z
- Metering event example: meter_event_id=me-88b3, org=lexi-1004, model=redwood-optimized-1.0, tokens=24123, price_tier=partner-rate, postback_status=ack
- Invoice line: invoice_2026_03_lexi_line_54, description='model-variant-rate-swap:partner-account', amount=2340.00 EUR
investigation_notes:
- Initial check: billing pipeline shows partner-rate attribution for ~18k tokens during the window.
- Routing: scheduler decision shows fallback rule fired due to 'preferred_pool_unavailable' metric. Policy file for lex i-1004 had an override flag mistakenly set true during an automated policy sync on 2026-02-28 22:05 UTC.
- Config drift: the org-level policy should have 'allow_partner_overflow=false'. Change was introduced by infra automation PR  a3f9b12 (linked).
- Postback system: postbacks for the routed requests were correctly delivered; metering pipeline used the assigned pool's rate table rather than the org's negotiated dedicated rates.
- Cross-check with account metadata: dedicated-reserved_tag present for 98% of other requests; these specific traces lacked reserved_tag because they were proxied through partner pool.
- Hypothesis: automation sync changed a boolean flag triggering fallback for this org during maintenance; billing pipeline then used partner rate table and charged partner surcharge.
customer_communication_thread: 2026-03-10 09:40 UTC - Aisha Patel (Support): 'Thanks for flagging this. We are investigating routing traces and billing attribution — we'll share an audit CSV and proposed credit by EOD 2026-03-12.'
2026-03-11 14:03 UTC - Marco Rivera (SRE): 'Found automation PR a3f9b12 toggled allow_partner_overflow on lex i-1004 during sync. Rolling back config for 2026-02-28 22:06 UTC. Preparing audit CSV.'

2026-03-11 18:21 UTC - LexiHealth Billing Contact (Emma S.): 'Please provide the raw CSV with meter_event_id, timestamp, model, token_count, routed_pool, and applied_rate. We need this for our procurement reconciliation.'
2026-03-12 08:55 UTC - Aisha Patel (Support): 'Audit CSV attached to ticket; draft credit of €2,340 proposed pending internal billing ops validation.'
resolution_notes:
- Immediate actions: Rolled back erroneous policy change and disabled the faulty automation job.
- Billing action: Draft credit of €2,340 created as provisional credit pending ledger reconciliation and finance sign-off. Credit reference: CR-LEXI-20260312-01.
- Delivered artifacts to customer: audit CSV (attached to ticket), routing trace snippets, and a link to the infra PR that caused the change.
- Preventative action: Added a validation gate to automation sync that prevents enabling partner overflow for orgs with dedicated-reserved_tag. Posting runbook update to confluence.
follow_up_items: 1) Finance: finalize and apply the provisional credit to LexiHealth's account and confirm final invoice adjustment (owner: @billing-team, due: 2026-03-15)
2) Infra: add unit test to automation sync ensuring org-level overrides are preserved for dedicated orgs (owner: @infra-automation, due: 2026-03-20)
3) Product: consider adding console warning when routing fallback is enabled for dedicated customers (owner: @product-billing, due: 2026-04-01)
4) CS: confirm with LexiHealth that backlog jobs are unpaused once credit applied (owner: Aisha Patel, due: 2026-03-13)
5) Postmortem: draft short postmortem for internal channel #incidents and link to this ticket (owner: Marco Rivera, due: 2026-03-18)
